easy.def: To stop.
examples: The rain ceased.
The noise will cease.
The music ceased.

more.def: To come to an end, or to stop doing something.
examples: The rain ceased at noon.
The noise ceased when the bell rang.
The factory ceased making toys.

easy.def: A tall tree with sweet-smelling wood.
examples: A cedar grows by our house.
The cedar smells so good.
Birds sit in the cedar.

more.def: A tall evergreen tree with sweet-smelling wood that is used to make chests, fences and closets.
examples: Grandma keeps blankets in a cedar chest because the wood smells fresh.
The tall cedar kept its green needles all winter long.
The fence around the garden is made of cedar.

easy.def: The top of a room.
examples: The lamp hangs from the ceiling.
The ceiling is white.
A fly is on the ceiling.

more.def: The flat surface that is the top of the inside of a room.
examples: A fan hung from the ceiling.
The ceiling of the church was painted blue.
The balloon floated up to the ceiling.

easy.def: To do something fun for a special day.
examples: We celebrate my birthday with cake.
We celebrate the new year with a party.
Let's celebrate! You lost a tooth!

more.def: To do something special or fun to mark a happy day or event.
examples: The team celebrated their win with a pizza party.
Many families celebrate holidays with special meals.
The town celebrated the opening of the new bridge.

easy.def: A party for a special day.
examples: We had a celebration.
The celebration was fun.
The birthday celebration was big.

more.def: An event or party that marks something special.
examples: We had a celebration for her birthday.
The town held a celebration after the big game.
The celebration ended with fireworks.

easy.def: For a party or joy.
examples: A celebratory cake.
The celebratory mood.
A celebratory song.

more.def: Done to celebrate something happy.
examples: They had a celebratory dinner after the win.
The celebratory mood filled the room.
A celebratory cake was served.

easy.def: A famous person.
examples: A celebrity visited.
The celebrity signed autographs.
She is a celebrity.

more.def: A person who is famous and known by many people.
examples: A celebrity visited our school.
The celebrity waved to the crowd.
Fans waited to see the celebrity.

easy.def: A long, green, crunchy vegetable.
examples: I ate celery.
The celery is crunchy.
Celery goes in soup.

more.def: A vegetable with long, crisp, pale green stalks that is eaten raw or cooked in soups and salads.
examples: I dipped a stalk of celery in peanut butter.
Celery is crunchy and full of water.
Mom added chopped celery to the chicken soup.

easy.def: Having to do with the sky or heaven.
examples: The moon is a celestial body.
A celestial map shows stars.
The celestial lights shone.

more.def: Having to do with the sky, outer space or heaven.
examples: The sun and moon are celestial objects.
We looked at a celestial map of the night sky.
A celestial glow filled the night sky.

easy.def: The tiny building block of living things.
examples: Your body is made of cells.
A cell is tiny.
Plants are made of cells.

more.def: The smallest part of a living thing, too tiny to see without a microscope.
examples: Your body is made of billions of cells.
We looked at an onion cell under the microscope.
A plant cell has a hard outer wall.

easy.def: A room under a house.
examples: The jam is in the cellar.
The cellar is cool.
We went down to the cellar.

more.def: An underground room below a house, often used to store things.
examples: Mom keeps jars of jam in the cellar.
The cellar is cool and dark.
We went down the stairs to the cellar.

easy.def: A person who plays the cello.
examples: A cellist plays the cello.
The cellist played.
She is a cellist.

more.def: A person who plays the cello.
examples: The cellist played a sad song.
She is the lead cellist in the orchestra.
A cellist sits to play the big instrument.

easy.def: A big instrument like a violin that you play sitting down.
examples: She plays the cello.
The cello sounds deep.
A cello is big.

more.def: A large string instrument that is played sitting down, with the instrument held between the knees and a bow drawn across its strings.
examples: She sat down and drew the bow across the strings of her cello.
The cello makes a deep, rich sound.
The orchestra has four cellos.

easy.def: A thin, clear wrap.
examples: The candy is in cellophane.
Cellophane is clear.
The gift had cellophane.

more.def: A thin, clear material used to wrap things.
examples: The candy was wrapped in crinkly cellophane.
A sheet of cellophane covered the basket.
Cellophane is thin and see-through.

easy.def: A phone you can carry anywhere.
examples: I have a cellphone.
A cellphone is small.
Mom called on the cellphone.

more.def: A phone that you can carry with you and use without wires.
examples: Mom called me on her cellphone.
A cellphone fits in your pocket.
He left his cellphone at home.

easy.def: A way to measure temperature.
examples: Ice melts at zero degrees Celsius.
It is twenty degrees Celsius.
Celsius is a scale.

more.def: A scale for measuring temperature in which water freezes at zero degrees and boils at one hundred.
examples: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
It was twenty degrees Celsius, a warm spring day.
Most countries use Celsius to say the temperature.

easy.def: A gray powder that becomes hard like stone when wet and dry.
examples: Workers mixed cement with water.
The cement is wet, so keep off.
We saw the truck pour cement.

more.def: A gray powder that is mixed with water and sand to make concrete, which hardens like rock.
examples: Builders mixed cement with sand and water to make a strong floor.
Wet cement is soft until it dries and turns hard.
The bridge is held together by cement and steel.

easy.def: To stick things together very hard.
examples: We cement the tiles to the floor.
Glue can cement a broken cup.
They cemented the stones in place.

more.def: To join things together firmly, as if with a strong glue.
examples: The workers cemented the bricks together to build the wall.
Playing games together cemented their friendship.
He cemented the broken piece of the statue back on.

easy.def: A place where people who have died are buried.
examples: The cemetery is quiet.
Flowers are in the cemetery.
The cemetery has stones.

more.def: A place where the bodies of dead people are buried, with stones to mark each grave.
examples: The cemetery was quiet and peaceful.
We left flowers at the cemetery.
The old cemetery had stone markers.

easy.def: To take out parts that are thought to be bad.
examples: They censor the film.
The words were censored.
The book was censored.

more.def: To remove parts of a book, a film or a message that someone thinks are not suitable or are not allowed.
examples: The TV station censored the bad words from the show.
The government censored the newspaper.
Some parts of the old book were censored.

easy.def: A count of all the people in a place.
examples: They took a census.
The census counts people.
The census was done.

more.def: An official count of all the people living in a place.
examples: The country takes a census every ten years.
The census showed how many people live in the town.
Workers counted the families for the census.

easy.def: A coin worth one hundredth of a dollar.
examples: A penny is one cent.
It costs fifty cents.
I found a cent.

more.def: A coin or amount of money equal to one hundredth of a dollar.
examples: A penny is worth one cent.
The gum costs fifty cents.
One hundred cents make a dollar.

easy.def: A make-believe creature that is half man and half horse.
examples: A centaur is in the story.
The centaur ran.
I drew a centaur.

more.def: A creature in old Greek stories that has the head and body of a man and the legs and body of a horse.
examples: A centaur is in the Greek story.
The centaur galloped through the woods.
I drew a centaur with a bow and a long, flowing tail.

easy.def: A hundredth birthday.
examples: The school's centennial.
A centennial party.
We celebrated the centennial.

more.def: The hundredth anniversary of an event.
examples: The town celebrated its centennial with a parade.
The school held a centennial party.
It was the centennial of the bridge.

easy.def: The middle.
examples: Stand in the center.
The center of the pizza is hot.
The center of the cookie is soft.

more.def: The point or part that is in the middle of something.
examples: Stand in the center of the circle.
The center of the flower is yellow.
The town square is in the center of the village.

easy.def: A building used for a special purpose.
examples: We play at the community center.
The art center has paints.
Mom works at the shopping center.

more.def: A building or place where people go for a particular activity or service.
examples: The science center has a planetarium.
We swim at the community center.
The shopping center has a toy shop.

easy.def: A decoration in the middle of a table.
examples: The centerpiece is flowers.
A centerpiece is on the table.
We made a centerpiece.

more.def: A decoration placed in the middle of a table.
examples: A bowl of flowers was the centerpiece on the table.
We made a centerpiece out of pumpkins.
The cake was the centerpiece of the party.

easy.def: A way to measure temperature.
examples: It is twenty degrees centigrade.
Water freezes at zero centigrade.
A centigrade scale.

more.def: Another name for Celsius, a scale for measuring temperature.
examples: Water freezes at zero degrees centigrade.
It was twenty-five degrees centigrade, a warm day.
The centigrade scale has one hundred degrees between freezing and boiling.

easy.def: A small unit of length, about the width of your fingernail.
examples: The bug is one centimeter long.
Measure in centimeters.
A centimeter is small.

more.def: A unit of length in the metric system, equal to one hundredth of a meter, about the width of a fingernail.
examples: The snail was about three centimeters long.
A ruler has centimeters marked along its edge.
There are one hundred centimeters in a meter.

easy.def: A long bug with many legs.
examples: A centipede crawled.
The centipede has many legs.
We saw a centipede.

more.def: A long, thin creature with a pair of legs on each part of its body.
examples: A centipede crawled under the rock.
Each section of a centipede's body has a pair of legs.
Centipedes hunt at night.

easy.def: In the middle.
examples: The central park is in the middle of the city.
The central room has a table.
The school is in a central place.

more.def: Near the middle of something, or most important.
examples: The central square has a fountain.
The town hall is in a central spot, easy for everyone to reach.
The main character is central to the story.

easy.def: A soldier long ago who led a group of soldiers.
examples: The centurion led his men.
A centurion was a Roman soldier.
The centurion marched.

more.def: An officer in the ancient Roman army who commanded about a hundred soldiers.
examples: The centurion led his men down the road.
A centurion wore a helmet with a tall crest.
The centurion gave orders to the soldiers.

easy.def: One hundred years.
examples: A century is a very long time.
The tree is a century old.
That house was built a century ago.

more.def: A period of one hundred years.
examples: Many castles were built more than a century ago.
The twentieth century began in the year 1901.
A hundred years make one century.

easy.def: A sea animal with a soft body and many arms.
examples: The cephalopod swims.
A squid is a cephalopod.
The cephalopod has eight arms.

more.def: A sea animal with a soft body, big eyes and many arms, such as an octopus or squid.
examples: An octopus is a cephalopod.
Cephalopods can squirt ink to escape.
The cephalopod changed color to hide.

easy.def: Made of clay that has been baked hard.
examples: We made a ceramic bowl.
The ceramic cup is white.
A ceramic pot sat there.

more.def: Made from clay that has been baked until it is hard.
examples: She painted a ceramic mug in art class.
A ceramic bowl sat on the shelf.
The ceramic tiles on the floor were cool.

easy.def: Things made from baked clay, or the craft of making them.
examples: I made ceramics.
Ceramics class is fun.
The shelf has ceramics.

more.def: Pots, bowls and other things made from clay that is baked hard, or the art of making them.
examples: We made bowls in ceramics class.
The museum has ceramics from long ago.
Her ceramics shone with blue paint.

easy.def: A breakfast food that you eat with milk.
examples: I eat cereal for breakfast.
The cereal is crunchy.
I poured milk on my cereal.

more.def: A food made from grains such as corn or wheat that is eaten with milk.
examples: A bowl of cereal and fruit is my usual breakfast.
She poured milk on her cereal.
The cereal was crunchy and sweet.

easy.def: Used for a special event.
examples: He wore a ceremonial robe.
They had a ceremonial dance.
The ceremonial cake was cut.

more.def: Used for or having to do with a ceremony, which is a special event.
examples: The chief wore a ceremonial headdress at the festival.
The mayor cut the ceremonial ribbon at the new park.
A ceremonial sword is carried in the parade.

easy.def: A special event with set actions.
examples: We went to the graduation ceremony.
The ceremony was on Sunday.
The ribbon-cutting ceremony was short.

more.def: A formal event with special words or actions to mark something important.
examples: The graduation ceremony was held in the gym.
The mayor cut a ribbon at the opening ceremony.
The medal ceremony took place after the race.

easy.def: Sure.
examples: I am certain it is Monday.
She is certain she locked the door.
Are you certain?

more.def: Completely sure about something.
examples: I am certain that I turned off the stove.
The scientist was certain the plan would work.
Are you certain this is the right path?

easy.def: Some, but not all.
examples: Certain plants need a lot of sun.
On certain days we have art.
Certain birds can talk.

more.def: Particular, but not named or said exactly.
examples: Certain animals sleep through the winter.
At certain times of the year, the river floods.
Certain mushrooms are dangerous to eat.

easy.def: Without any doubt.
examples: That is certainly a big dog.
I will certainly come.
It certainly is cold today.

more.def: Without any doubt; for sure.
examples: That is certainly the biggest pumpkin I have ever seen.
I will certainly be there on time.
It was certainly a surprise to see snow in May.

easy.def: Something that is sure to happen.
examples: Rain is a certainty today.
It is a certainty that I will win.
She spoke with certainty.

more.def: The feeling of being completely sure, or something that is sure to happen.
examples: She spoke with certainty, because she had checked the answer twice.
It was a certainty that the sun would rise the next morning.
There is no certainty that the game will be played if it rains.

easy.def: A paper that proves something.
examples: I got a certificate for reading.
The certificate is framed.
My certificate has my name.

more.def: An official paper that shows that something is true or that you have done something.
examples: I got a certificate for reading ten books.
Her birth certificate has the date she was born.
The swimmers received a certificate.

easy.def: Proved by a paper to be good or true.
examples: She is a certified teacher.
The certified lifeguard watched the pool.
The seeds are certified.

more.def: Officially proved or approved by a paper or a test, to show someone has the right training or something meets a standard.
examples: A certified lifeguard watched the swimmers at the pool.
The food is certified organic, so it follows special farming rules.
Mom is a certified teacher with a paper from the state.

easy.def: To say officially that something is true.
examples: The teacher certified it.
They certify the winner.
The doctor certified her.

more.def: To officially confirm that something is true or meets a standard.
examples: The inspector certified the bridge as safe.
The teacher certified that she had finished.
The paper certified that he passed.

easy.def: A whale, dolphin or porpoise.
examples: A whale is a cetacean.
Cetaceans live in the sea.
The cetacean swam.

more.def: A sea animal such as a whale or dolphin.
examples: A whale is a cetacean that breathes air.
Cetaceans communicate with clicks and songs.
We watched a pod of cetaceans leap from the water.
